summary: The body-width implementation and focused tests provide deterministic coverage for subpixel chord measurement, endpoint trimming, unavailable behavior, rotation stability, representative-plane selection, and explicit legacy-field separation. The apparent-width limitation is documented in the claim registry.

evidence: `tests/test_saturn_v571_body_width.py:58-74` covers known-width rotated rectangles at five angles.
`tests/test_saturn_v571_body_width.py:76-100` verifies endpoint trimming against a tapered synthetic mask.
`tests/test_saturn_v571_body_width.py:139-151` verifies insufficient samples return NaN rather than fabricated width.
`tests/test_saturn_v571_body_width.py:153-180` verifies largest-area Z-plane selection rather than widest-plane selection.
`tests/test_saturn_v571_body_width.py:203-226` verifies primary body-width summary fields and explicitly labelled legacy EDT fields.
`audits/claims_registry.json:89-107` records the acceptance criteria and apparent-width/PSF limitations.
`sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:3519-3529` propagates unavailable body width as NaN and avoids calculating the primary ratio from non-finite width.
`sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:3554-3561` assigns explicit length review bands without converting morphology into technical failure.
`audits/validation/v571_6f9e73b_validation.md:16-29` records a passing 229-test validation, but it targets commit `6f9e73b`, not the reviewed commit.
No full stack or fresh pytest execution was run under this read-only review.

limitations: This review assessed source, tests, schemas, and retained artifacts without running the full pipeline.
The retained validation receipt predates the reviewed commit, although the requested body-width test and implementation evidence are present at the reviewed commit.
recommended_follow_up: Run the focused body-width pytest module at the reviewed commit in a writable validated environment.
